title: Add DB migration sandbox, operator eviction guard, and tenant safelist for private upgrades
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a non-destructive DB migration sandbox and an admission-style eviction guard for the private installer operator. Enables a tenant safelist and dry-run reporting for schema migrations; no behavioral change by default unless flags enabled.
description:
Summary: Introduces a migration sandbox mode and operator eviction guard to reduce blast radius during private upgrades. Adds a tenant safelist (opt-in per-cluster) and a dry-run reporting pipeline for SQL/DDL migrations so operators can validate changes end-to-end before committing. Motivation: customers running Redwood Private have reported upgrade incidents where long-running schema migrations caused operator eviction/failover and tenant-impacting rollbacks. This PR provides a safe rehearsal path and automated rollback hooks to make upgrades incremental and observable.

What changed (high-level): \u2022 migration-sandbox controller: new controller that spins up ephemeral migration workers in a fenced namespace to run schema migrations against a writable but isolated sandbox DB (Postgres logical replica + rewrite rules). Outputs a detailed migration report (timings, locks, sample queries) to a ClusterReport custom resource. \u2022 operator-eviction guard: admission-style hook that blocks eviction or scaling down of critical operator/statefulset pods when an in-flight migration with a "lock-sensitive" label exists in the cluster. Guard can be overridden by explicit force-unblock from admins. \u2022 tenant-safelist: cluster-scoped config map + CRD allowing operators to mark tenants (namespaces/tenanted IDs) that are excluded from disruptive migration strategies during a rollout. \u2022 dry-run pipeline: SQL parser + preflight check stage that detects potential locking patterns (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, ALTER TABLE ...), estimates lock durations using sampling, and emits recommendations (CONCURRENTLY, chunked index build, background migration). \u2022 UX: console annotations and installer CLI flags: --enable-migration-sandbox, --migration-safelist-file, --dry-run-report-path.

Commits (summary): \u2022 1a2b3c4: scaffold migration-sandbox controller and CRDs\u2022 2b3c4d5: implement logical-replica executor + report generator\u2022 3c4d5e6: admission webhook for operator-eviction guard\u2022 4d5e6f7: tenant-safelist CRD and CLI wiring\u2022 5e6f7g8: dry-run SQL analysis engine and unit tests\u2022 6f7g8h9: e2e smoke tests and install docs

Files changed (representative): \u2022 charts/private-installer/templates/migration-sandbox.yaml (adds CRDs + controller deployment)\u2022 operator/controllers/migration_sandbox_controller.go (controller logic + reconcile loop)\u2022 operator/webhook/eviction_guard.go (admission webhook)\u2022 pkg/migration/dryrun/parser.go (SQL heuristics)\u2022 cli/install/migration_flags.go (installer flags)\u2022 docs/private-upgrades/migration-sandbox.md (operator runbook + playbook)

Small illustrative snippet (controller reconcile loop, simplified): \n```\n// reconcile: ensure sandbox job exists for the migration CR\nif !sandboxJobExists(cr) {\n  job := buildSandboxJob(cr)\n  r.client.Create(ctx, job)\n}\n// watch job status -> generate ClusterReport when finished\n```\n\nTesting and CI: The PR adds unit tests for the SQL heuristics, controller integration tests using KIND, and an e2e smoke job in the CI pipeline that validates CRD install/uninstall across supported K8s versions. CI initially failed on a flaky interaction between the webhook and the controller; fixed by adding a short backoff and idempotent admission response. Final CI status: pass (all checks green after rerun).

Review conversation (excerpt): \u2022 Jonas Becker (reviewer, 2025-11-18): "Nice isolation approach. Two asks: 1) add a TTL/garbage collection policy for sandbox DBs, and 2) ensure reports avoid PII in sample rows." \u2022 Maya Patel (author): "Added sandbox TTL config and implemented redaction hooks for sample rows (see pkg/migration/report_redact.go)." \u2022 Priya Singh (reviewer): "Eviction guard looks safe but we need an operator-level override for emergencies; suggest 'force-unblock' on the Operator CR." \u2022 Maya Patel: "Added operator.forceUnblock field and CLI admin command 'redwoodctl admin unblock-operator --reason'. Documented audit log entry." \u2022 Carlos Ramirez (approver): "E2E passed in my local cluster, and dry-run reports are useful for SRE teams. Approved with nits." \u2022 Post-merge note from SRE (internal): "Recommend enabling sandbox non-disruptively on staging clusters for 2 weeks before canarying to production. Added Linear ticket ENG-1610 for rollout plan." 

Backward compatibility and safety: The migration sandbox and safelist are opt-in behind installer flags and Operator CR fields. Default behavior of upgrades remains unchanged unless cluster admin enables the sandbox. The eviction guard only blocks automated eviction paths; manual admin overrides are available.

Operational runbook (short): \u2022 Stage: enable --enable-migration-sandbox on a staging cluster and run existing migration manifests with --dry-run-report-path set. Review ClusterReport for lock warnings. \u2022 Canary: enable safelist to exclude high-risk tenants, run migrations in sandbox for the rest. \u2022 Production: once reports are clean, flip migration-controller to 'apply' mode. If the eviction guard blocks a rollout, use 'redwoodctl admin unblock-operator' with a documented reason and follow rollback steps described in docs.

Why this is different from prior work: Earlier PRs focused on atomic rollback and snapshot restore; this PR focuses on preflight and rehearsal for schema changes and prevents operator-level disruption during migrations. It reduces human error during upgrades by giving teams a repeatable, observable dry-run and a mitigated path to production.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals from Jonas, Priya, and Carlos. Changelog entry and upgrade notes added to docs site.

Follow-ups: ENG-1610 (rollout plan + monitoring), ENG-1623 (add anonymized cost-estimation for long-running migrations), DOC-78 (console integration for ClusterReport).
